previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, multiple prior stents, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, type 2 diabetes, and antiphospholipid syndrome presented with chest pain during a scheduled endoscopy, found to have an aborted inferior STEMI. Initial evaluation showed subtherapeutic INR of 1.4 and normal initial troponin, which later peaked at 0.16. Coronary angiography revealed stable coronary anatomy with no new intervenable lesions. He was managed with heparin infusion and transitioned to warfarin 6 mg daily, with continuation of dual antiplatelet therapy. His metoprolol was reduced to 150 mg and valsartan to 80 mg due to orthostasis, and diltiazem was discontinued. Insulin was adjusted for glucose control. He remained stable, with INR reaching 2.5 at discharge. He was discharged home on optimized medical therapy with follow-up planned in primary care, cardiology, and anticoagulation clinics.

Brief Hospital Course:
PATIENT SUMMARY:
================
___ with PMH of HTN, DM, APLS, and CAD s/p multiple caths and 
stents, who presents with substernal chest pain on exertion that 
sounds similar to his stable angina. Also with complaints of 
abdominal pain worse in the epigastrium.

ACUTE ISSUES:
=============
# Stable angina:
The patient presented with substernal chest pain/pressure on 
walking that was similar to the chest pain he gets almost every 
time he walks. This particular episode may have been a little 
worse, but he did not have his SL nitro with him so he sat down 
and it improved after about 15 minutes. He was on his way to his 
arterial duplex study, and when he arrived and told them of this 
episode, they sent him to the ED. Trops were negative x3 and he 
had no EKG changes from his baseline. Initially there was 
concern for unstable angina given his history and so he was 
given ASA 324mg and started on a nitro gtt as well as a heparin 
gtt with resolution of his pain. When the nitro gtt was stopped, 
he did not have recurrence of the pain and remained chest pain 
free for the duration of his hospitalization. He had an ETT on 
___ which revealed no angina or ischemic EKG changes. Exercise 
was stopped due to fatigue at a low workload. In this setting, 
heparin gtt was stopped and he was started on Imdur 30mg daily. 
His plavix 75mg daily, atorvastatin 80mg, and metoprolol 
succinate 150mg were continued. His ASA 81mg daily was d/c in 
the setting of him already being on Plavix and xarelto with a 
questionable history of UGIB. Further discussions to be had with 
outpatient cardiologist re: necessity of ASA (last DES in LAD on 
___.

# Abdominal pain:
This is an ongoing issue that is being worked up by his PCP and 
GI. ___ abdominal pain appears to be unrelated to his chest 
pain. He describes it as a heaviness/pressure that sometimes 
improves with eating; denies nausea, vomiting, reflux/heartburn, 
regurgitation. His pain improved somewhat with Maalox, 
Simethicone, and calcium carbonate. He also has a history of 
constipation as an outpatient for which he is on multiple bowel 
meds. He had a normal EGD ___ with normal gastric biopsies 
which is reassuring. He is scheduled for outpatient GI follow-up 
in the coming weeks and has CT Abd scheduled for ___. Can 
continue further workup as an outpatient.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
==============
# Antiphospholipid syndrome:
Patient was initially on heparin gtt, and when that was d/c he 
was restarted on his home xarelto. It was noted that he is on 
triple therapy (ASA, Plavix, xarelto) and in setting of 
questionable UGIB his ASA was stopped. Recent HemOnc note 
reported OK with stopping ASA given no evidence to support 
triple therapy in APLS.

# HFpEF: 
Per last discharge summary he takes his Lasix 40mg as a prn at 
home
for weight gain. He appeared euvolemic on exam throughout 
hospitalization and did not require any diuretic. His metoprolol 
succinate 150mg daily was continued.

# T2DM: 
At home on Glargine 46U with breakfast and dinner; Humalog 14U 
with breakfast, 16U with lunch, 14U with dinner plus ISS. Here 
he was on reduced dose glargine 35U with breakfast and dinner 
and Humalog ISS given initially NPO. Will be discharged on home 
regimen as well as home Metformin (which was held in inpatient 
setting).

# HTN:
Continued home losartan 100mg daily.

# Pancytopenia:
Has had intermittent leukopenia and thrombocytopenia in the past 
which has recovered spontaneously, although he is currently 
being worked up for anemia as an outpatient. The biggest concern 
as an
outpatient was for UGIB, but he had a normal EGD ___ which is 
reassuring. As he is having an ongoing workup as an outpatient 
no further workup done. WBC stable ~4, Hgb stable ___, Plt 
stable 110s-120s.

# Hypothyroidism: 
Continued home levothyroxine 112mcg daily.

# Chronic pain: 
Continued home pregabalin 150mg BID and oxycodone 5mg q8h prn.

# GERD:
Home esomeprazole 40mg BID was switched to Protonix 40mg daily 
inpatient, but he can take his Nexium at home.

===================

hospitalization.
